Large healthcare systems enrolling new provider NPIs for existing operational locations

title: Single-Code Billing Concentration and Impossible Day Healthcare Fraud
description: Detects two high-confidence healthcare billing fraud indicators: (1) Single-code billing concentration — providers billing overwhelmingly one HCPCS/CPT code, where a single code exceeds 80% of total claims. Operation Gold Rush documented a TCO that submitted $10.6 billion in fraudulent claims concentrated on urinary catheters and continuous glucose monitors. Legitimate providers bill across diverse code sets reflecting varied patient needs. (2) Impossible day billing — providers billing more than 24 hours of procedures in a single calendar day, a mathematical impossibility indicating phantom billing or systematic upcoding. Both patterns are documented in DOJ 2025 National Healthcare Fraud Takedown prosecutions and CrimsonVector Security threat analysis. Source: CrimsonVector Security March 2026; DOJ Operation Gold Rush June 2025.

enrichment_required.source: CMS HCPCS code time estimates (standard procedure duration mapping)
CMS provider specialty billing statistics (peer comparison baseline)

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Single-Code Billing Concentration Detection")`
`comment("Flags providers where one HCPCS code exceeds 80% of total claims")`
index=medicare_claims sourcetype=cms_claims
| stats
    count AS total_claims
    sum(billed_amount) AS total_billed
    dc(beneficiary_id) AS unique_beneficiaries
    dc(hcpcs_code) AS unique_codes
  by provider_npi
| where total_claims >= 500
| eval code_diversity=round(unique_codes/total_claims, 4)
| where code_diversity < 0.05
| join type=inner max=0 provider_npi [search index=medicare_claims sourcetype=cms_claims
  | stats count AS code_count by provider_npi, hcpcs_code
  | eventstats sum(code_count) AS provider_total by provider_npi
  | eval code_pct=round(code_count/provider_total*100, 1)
  | where code_pct > 80
  | fields provider_npi, hcpcs_code, code_pct]
| sort -total_billed
| eval alert_type="SINGLE_CODE_CONCENTRATION"

`comment("--- Detection 2: Impossible Day Billing ---")`
`comment("Flags providers billing more than 24 hours of procedures per day")`
index=medicare_claims sourcetype=cms_claims
| lookup hcpcs_time_estimates hcpcs_code OUTPUT estimated_minutes
| stats
    sum(estimated_minutes) AS total_minutes
    count AS claim_count
    dc(beneficiary_id) AS patients_per_day
    sum(billed_amount) AS daily_billed
  by provider_npi, service_date
| where total_minutes > 1440
| eval hours_billed=round(total_minutes/60, 1)
| eval alert_type="IMPOSSIBLE_DAY"
| sort -total_minutes
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Single-Code Billing Concentration Detection
WITH provider_code_stats AS (
  SELECT
    provider_npi,
    hcpcs_code,
    COUNT(*) AS code_claims,
    SUM(billed_amount) AS code_billed,
    SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY provider_npi) AS total_claims,
    SUM(SUM(billed_amount)) OVER (PARTITION BY provider_npi) AS total_billed
  FROM claims
  WHERE service_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
  GROUP BY provider_npi, hcpcs_code
)
SELECT
  provider_npi,
  hcpcs_code AS dominant_code,
  code_claims,
  total_claims,
  ROUND(code_claims::numeric / total_claims * 100, 1) AS code_pct,
  total_billed,
  'SINGLE_CODE_CONCENTRATION' AS alert_type
FROM provider_code_stats
WHERE total_claims >= 500
  AND ROUND(code_claims::numeric / total_claims * 100, 1) > 80
ORDER BY total_billed DESC;

-- SQL for Impossible Day Billing Detection
SELECT
  c.provider_npi,
  p.provider_name,
  c.service_date,
  SUM(h.estimated_minutes) AS total_minutes_billed,
  ROUND(SUM(h.estimated_minutes) / 60.0, 1) AS hours_billed,
  COUNT(*) AS claim_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.beneficiary_id) AS patients,
  SUM(c.billed_amount) AS daily_billed
FROM claims c
JOIN hcpcs_time_estimates h ON c.hcpcs_code = h.hcpcs_code
JOIN providers p ON c.provider_npi = p.provider_npi
WHERE c.service_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
GROUP BY c.provider_npi, p.provider_name, c.service_date
HAVING SUM(h.estimated_minutes) > 1440
ORDER BY total_minutes_billed DESC;

falsepositives: Large group practices billing under a single NPI (though this should be identified via provider type in PECOS)
DME suppliers legitimately specializing in a narrow product category (e.g., CPAP-only suppliers) — though even specialists typically bill multiple related codes

title: Ghost Patient Claims and Geographic Provider Clustering Detection
description: Detects two healthcare fraud patterns: (1) Ghost patient claims — Medicare/Medicaid claims submitted for deceased, incarcerated, or relocated beneficiaries who could not have received the billed services. Operation Gold Rush exploited over 1 million stolen American identities including elderly and disabled individuals. (2) Geographic provider clustering — ZIP codes with anomalous concentrations of healthcare providers and high average billing per provider, indicating shell company clustering. LA County has 1,923 registered hospice providers (more than 36 states combined), with 7 of 14 entities in one LA plaza having zero CMS data. GAO reports found approximately 22% of practice locations in PECOS were potentially ineligible including UPS Store mailboxes and vacant addresses. Source: CrimsonVector Security March 2026; DOJ 2025 National Healthcare Fraud Takedown; GAO-15-448.

enrichment_required.source: CMS beneficiary eligibility records (death, incarceration, relocation status)
USPS Commercial Mail Receiving Agency database cross-reference

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Ghost Patient Claims Detection")`
`comment("Identifies claims submitted for deceased or incarcerated beneficiaries")`
index=medicare_claims sourcetype=cms_claims
| join type=inner max=0 beneficiary_id [search index=beneficiary_eligibility
  | where beneficiary_status IN ("deceased", "incarcerated")
  | fields beneficiary_id beneficiary_status status_effective_date]
| eval claim_date_epoch=strptime(service_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
| eval status_date_epoch=strptime(status_effective_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
| where claim_date_epoch > status_date_epoch
| stats
    count AS ghost_claims
    sum(billed_amount) AS ghost_billed
    dc(beneficiary_id) AS ghost_beneficiaries
    values(beneficiary_status) AS status_types
  by provider_npi
| where ghost_claims > 5
| sort -ghost_billed

`comment("--- Detection 2: Geographic Provider Clustering ---")`
`comment("Identifies ZIP codes with anomalous provider density and billing")`
index=pecos_enrollment sourcetype=cms_enrollment
| stats
    dc(provider_npi) AS provider_count
    values(provider_name) AS providers
  by provider_zip, provider_type
| where provider_count >= 10
| join type=inner max=0 provider_zip [search index=medicare_claims sourcetype=cms_claims
  | stats sum(billed_amount) AS total_zip_billed dc(provider_npi) AS billing_providers by provider_zip
  | eval avg_billing_per_provider=round(total_zip_billed/billing_providers, 2)]
| where avg_billing_per_provider > 500000
| eval alert_type="GEOGRAPHIC_CLUSTERING"
| sort -provider_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Ghost Patient Claims Detection
SELECT
  c.provider_npi,
  p.provider_name,
  COUNT(*) AS ghost_claims,
  SUM(c.billed_amount) AS ghost_billed,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.beneficiary_id) AS ghost_beneficiaries,
  b.beneficiary_status
FROM claims c
JOIN beneficiary_eligibility b ON c.beneficiary_id = b.beneficiary_id
JOIN providers p ON c.provider_npi = p.provider_npi
WHERE b.beneficiary_status IN ('deceased', 'incarcerated')
  AND c.service_date > b.status_effective_date
  AND c.service_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
GROUP BY c.provider_npi, p.provider_name, b.beneficiary_status
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
ORDER BY ghost_billed DESC;

-- SQL for Geographic Provider Clustering Detection
SELECT
  e.provider_zip,
  e.provider_type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT e.provider_npi) AS provider_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(c.billed_amount), 0) AS total_zip_billed,
  ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(c.billed_amount), 0)::numeric
    / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT e.provider_npi), 0), 2) AS avg_billing_per_provider,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN addr.address_type = 'CMRA' THEN e.provider_npi END) AS cmra_addresses,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN addr.address_type = 'residential' THEN e.provider_npi END) AS residential_addresses
FROM provider_enrollment e
LEFT JOIN claims c ON e.provider_npi = c.provider_npi
  AND c.service_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '365 days'
LEFT JOIN address_classification addr ON e.physical_address = addr.address
WHERE e.provider_type IN ('hospice', 'home_health', 'dme', 'aba_therapy')
GROUP BY e.provider_zip, e.provider_type
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.provider_npi) >= 10
   AND ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(c.billed_amount), 0)::numeric
    / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT e.provider_npi), 0), 2) > 500000
ORDER BY provider_count DESC;

falsepositives: Claims submitted with processing delays where beneficiary status changed after service but before claim adjudication
Legitimate healthcare clusters in medical districts or hospital complexes
Large home health agencies serving wide geographic areas from a central office

title: Recovery Fraud Contact Pattern — Payments from Recent Fraud Victims to Unfamiliar Recipients
description: Detects potential recovery fraud by identifying payments from customers who filed fraud complaints within the preceding 90 days to previously unseen recipient accounts. Recovery fraud operators re-contact prior fraud victims posing as recovery agents, lawyers, or government officials, extracting additional fees for purported fund recovery. This rule correlates complaint records with subsequent outbound payment activity to flag secondary victimization.

`comment("Cross-references fraud complaints with subsequent outbound payments to new recipients")`

| join type=inner max=0 customer_id [
  search index=flame_fraud sourcetype=flame:complaints
  | where complaint_date >= relative_time(now(), "-90d")
  | fields customer_id, complaint_date, original_loss_amount, fraud_type
]
| search NOT [
  search index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:transaction_monitoring
    transaction_type IN ("WIRE_OUT", "ACH_OUT", "CRYPTO_TRANSFER")
    transaction_date < complaint_date
  | dedup recipient_account, customer_id
  | fields recipient_account, customer_id

  BY customer_id, fraud_type, original_loss_amount

transaction_type IN ["WIRE_OUT", "ACH_OUT", "CRYPTO_TRANSFER"]

-- SQL for Recovery Fraud Contact Pattern
SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    t.transaction_date,
    t.amount,
    t.recipient_account,
    c.complaint_date,
    c.original_loss_amount,

This rule identifies inbound calling patterns characteristic of organized boiler room operations, including sequential source number prefixes, short call duration clustering, and geographic origin mismatch between caller ID display and actual call routing.

title: Long-Firm Credit Buildup Pattern — Steady Low Utilization Followed by Rapid Spike
description: Detects commercial accounts following a long-firm fraud pattern: steady low-value credit utilization for 6-12 months (building creditworthiness) followed by rapid escalation in credit utilization (the "burst"). Long-firm fraud involves organized criminal groups establishing businesses, building credit relationships, then exploiting that trust to defraud supply chain partners and trade finance banks. The artificially smooth buildup period followed by a discontinuous spike is the hallmark behavioral indicator.

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Long-Firm Credit Buildup Pattern
// Detects steady low utilization followed by rapid credit spike
account_type="commercial"
| bucket(field=@timestamp, span=1mon)
| groupBy([account_id, @timestamp], function=[
    avg(credit_utilization_pct, as=avg_util),
    max(credit_utilization_pct, as=max_util)
  ])
| window(function=[avg(avg_util, as=trailing_6m_avg)], by=account_id, order=@timestamp, rows=[-6, -1])
| window(function=[collect(avg_util, as=prev_month_util)], by=account_id, order=@timestamp, rows=[-1, -1])
| trailing_6m_avg < 35 AND avg_util > 80 AND prev_month_util < 50
| sort(avg_util, order=desc)

`comment("Splunk SPL for Long-Firm Credit Buildup Pattern")`
`comment("Detects steady low utilization followed by rapid credit spike")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:commercial_credit account_type="commercial"
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats avg(credit_utilization_pct) AS avg_util,
        max(credit_utilization_pct) AS max_util
  BY account_id, _time
| streamstats avg(avg_util) AS trailing_6m_avg,
              current=false window=6
  BY account_id
| streamstats latest(avg_util) AS prev_month_util,

  BY account_id

queries.sql:
-- SQL for Long-Firm Credit Buildup Pattern
WITH monthly_util AS (
    SELECT
        account_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date) AS month,
        AVG(credit_utilization_pct) AS avg_util
    FROM commercial_credit_accounts
    WHERE account_type = 'commercial'
    GROUP BY account_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', transaction_date)
),
trend AS (
    SELECT
        account_id,
        month,
        avg_util,
        LAG(avg_util, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY month) AS prev_month_util,
        AVG(avg_util) OVER (
            PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY month
            ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
        ) AS trailing_6m_avg
    FROM monthly_util
)
SELECT account_id, month, avg_util, trailing_6m_avg, prev_month_util
FROM trend
WHERE trailing_6m_avg < 35
  AND avg_util > 80
  AND prev_month_util < 50
ORDER BY month DESC

title: Staged Accident Claim Correlation — Shared Professional Enabler Network Detection
description: Detects potential organized crash-for-cash insurance fraud rings by identifying claims from multiple ostensibly unrelated accidents that share common professional enablers (same medical provider, legal representative, or repair shop). Organized insurance fraud rings rely on networks of corrupt professionals who process claims across multiple staged incidents. The shared professional enabler network is the most durable and detectable element of the ring, as replacing trusted corrupt professionals is harder than recruiting new participants.

`comment("Identifies claims sharing professional enablers across unrelated accidents")`

| eval claim_date_epoch=strptime(claim_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
| where claim_date_epoch > relative_time(now(), "-365d")
| stats dc(accident_id) AS accident_count,
        dc(claim_id) AS claim_count,
        values(accident_id) AS accidents,
        sum(claim_amount) AS total_claimed
  BY medical_provider
| where accident_count >= 3

    BY legal_representative

]

-- SQL for Staged Accident Claim Correlation
-- Identifies shared professional enablers across unrelated accidents
SELECT
    'medical' AS provider_type,
    a.medical_provider AS shared_provider,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) AS accident_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.claim_id) AS claim_count,
    SUM(a.claim_amount) AS total_claimed
FROM insurance_claims a
WHERE a.claim_type = 'vehicle_accident'
  AND a.claim_date >= DATEADD(year, -1, GETDATE())
  AND a.medical_provider IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.medical_provider
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.accident_id) >= 3

UNION ALL

SELECT
    'legal' AS provider_type,
    a.legal_representative AS shared_provider,

# Each principle scored 0.0-1.0 based on linguistic markers

    'social_proof': ['everyone is', 'thousands of people', 'most popular',

    'authority': ['official notice', 'government', 'compliance required',
                 'legal obligation', 'regulatory', 'certified', 'verified'],
    'liking': ['dear friend', 'I care about you', 'we have so much in common',
              'I trust you', 'you are special', 'between us'],
    'scarcity': ['limited time', 'only X left', 'expires today',
                'final chance', 'act now', 'once in a lifetime', 'exclusive']
}

def score_cialdini_principles(text):
    scores = {}
    for principle, markers in PRINCIPLE_MARKERS.items():
        # Marker count + SBERT semantic similarity to principle exemplars
        marker_hits = sum(1 for m in markers if m.lower() in text.lower())
        semantic_sim = sbert_similarity(text, principle_exemplars[principle])
        scores[principle] = min(1.0, (marker_hits * 0.2) + (semantic_sim * 0.6))

title: Smishing Triad Domain Pattern and iMessage/RCS Delivery Detection
description: Detects indicators of Smishing Triad phishing infrastructure including Darcula/Magic Cat domain patterns and Chenlun kit fingerprints. The Smishing Triad ecosystem has generated 194,000+ malicious domains targeting users in 121+ countries, compromising 884,000+ credit cards. Darcula domains follow a "com-" prefix pattern. Chenlun kits are fingerprinted by the presence of ResourceRedConfig.js and /ResourceConfig/urlConfig.json files. Detection also covers toll-scam lure patterns (E-ZPass, SunPass, FasTrak, I-Pass) commonly used in smishing campaigns.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Smishing Triad Domain Pattern Detection")`
`comment("Matches Darcula com- prefix, Chenlun kit files, and toll-scam lures")`
index=web sourcetype=proxy:access
| eval smishing_indicator = case(
    match(url, "^https?://com-[a-z0-9]+"), "darcula_domain_pattern",
    match(url, "ResourceRedConfig\.js"), "chenlun_kit_fingerprint",
    match(url, "/ResourceConfig/urlConfig\.json"), "chenlun_kit_fingerprint",
    match(url, "(?i)(ezpass|sunpass|fastrak|ipass|toll-|parking-notice)"), "toll_scam_lure",
    1=1, null()
  )
| where isnotnull(smishing_indicator)
| lookup domain_age_lookup domain OUTPUT domain_age_days
| where domain_age_days < 30 OR isnull(domain_age_days)
| stats count BY smishing_indicator, domain, source_ip, url
| sort - count
queries.sql:
-- SQL: Smishing Triad domain pattern detection
-- Correlates proxy logs with domain intelligence
SELECT
    p.access_time,
    p.source_ip,
    p.url,
    p.domain,
    d.registration_date,
    DATEDIFF(day, d.registration_date, GETDATE()) AS domain_age_days,
    CASE
        WHEN p.domain LIKE 'com-%' THEN 'darcula_domain_pattern'
        WHEN p.url LIKE '%ResourceRedConfig.js%' THEN 'chenlun_kit_fingerprint'
        WHEN p.url LIKE '%/ResourceConfig/urlConfig.json%' THEN 'chenlun_kit_fingerprint'
        WHEN p.url LIKE '%ezpass%' OR p.url LIKE '%sunpass%'
            OR p.url LIKE '%fastrak%' OR p.url LIKE '%ipass%' THEN 'toll_scam_lure'
    END AS indicator_type
FROM proxy_access_logs p
LEFT JOIN domain_intelligence d ON p.domain = d.domain
WHERE (p.domain LIKE 'com-%'
       OR p.url LIKE '%ResourceRedConfig.js%'
       OR p.url LIKE '%/ResourceConfig/urlConfig.json%'
       OR p.url LIKE '%ezpass%' OR p.url LIKE '%sunpass%'
       OR p.url LIKE '%fastrak%' OR p.url LIKE '%ipass%')
  AND p.access_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, GETDATE())
ORDER BY p.access_time DESC

title: Synthetic Identity Credit Utilization Spike — Low-and-Slow Buildup Followed by Bust-Out
description: Detects the characteristic synthetic identity bust-out pattern: prolonged low credit utilization (< 35% for 6+ months) followed by a rapid spike to near-maximum utilization (> 80%) within 30 days. Synthetic identity fraudsters nurture credit profiles over 12-24 months with steady payments and low utilization, then execute a coordinated bust-out where all available credit is maxed simultaneously. The Federal Reserve estimates synthetic identity fraud costs U.S. lenders $6B+ annually. The discontinuous utilization jump from a stable baseline is the hallmark behavioral indicator.

Prior month-end utilization snapshot

(account_type="consumer_credit" OR account_type="credit_card")
trailing_6m_avg_utilization_pct<35
current_utilization_pct>=80
previous_month_utilization_pct<50
| utilization_jump_pct := current_utilization_pct - previous_month_utilization_pct
| months_at_low_utilization := payment_history_months
| groupBy(account_id, function=[
    collect([credit_limit, current_balance, current_utilization_pct,
             trailing_6m_avg_utilization_pct, utilization_jump_pct,

SELECT

title: Thin-File Identity Clustering — Shared Address, Phone, or Device Across New Applicants
description: Detects clusters of thin-file credit applicants sharing physical addresses, phone numbers, or device fingerprints — a hallmark indicator of synthetic identity ring activity. Fraud rings fabricate multiple synthetic identities that share infrastructure (mailing addresses, burner phones, devices used for applications). When 3+ new applicants with thin credit files (< 12 months history, < 3 tradelines) share an address, phone, or device within a 180-day window, this indicates coordinated identity fabrication rather than coincidental overlap. The Federal Reserve identifies address and device clustering as primary synthetic identity detection signals.

detection.condition: count(distinct applicant_id) by shared_attribute >= 3 where shared_attribute in (address, phone, device_fingerprint) within 180 days AND selection_thin_file

| stats dc(applicant_id) AS applicant_count,
        values(applicant_id) AS applicants,
        values(phone) AS phones,
        values(device_fingerprint) AS devices,
        values(ssn_hash) AS ssn_hashes,
        min(application_date) AS first_app,

  BY address
| where applicant_count >= 3
| eval days_span = round((strptime(last_app, "%Y-%m-%d") - strptime(first_app, "%Y-%m-%d")) / 86400)
| where days_span <= 180
| eval shared_attribute = "address"

  STRING_AGG(a.applicant_id, ', ') AS applicants,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.phone, ', ') AS phones,

FROM credit_applications a
WHERE a.credit_history_months < 12
  AND a.tradeline_count < 3
  AND a.application_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -180, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY a.address
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_id) >= 3
ORDER BY applicant_count DESC

description: Detects credit applications where the SSN characteristics are inconsistent with the applicant's stated identity — a primary indicator of synthetic identity fabrication. -- Detects repeated liveness failures followed by success from same device
WITH liveness_stats AS (
  SELECT
    l.device_fingerprint,
    l.applicant_id,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN l.liveness_result = 'fail' THEN 1 END) AS failure_count,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN l.liveness_result = 'pass' THEN 1 END) AS success_count,
    MIN(l.liveness_timestamp) AS first_attempt,

  GROUP BY l.device_fingerprint, l.applicant_id
)
SELECT
  device_fingerprint,
  applicant_id,
  failure_count,
  success_count,
  first_attempt,
  last_attempt,
  time_window_hours,
  score_history
FROM liveness_stats
WHERE failure_count >= 3
  AND success_count >= 1
  AND time_window_hours <= 24

title: Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly with Subsequent Account Changes
description: Detects financial institution employees accessing customer accounts outside their normal behavioral pattern, combined with subsequent account modifications — a hallmark of insider- enabled fraud. The rule identifies four converging anomaly signals: (1) account access occurring outside normal business hours for the employee's role, (2) access volume significantly exceeding the employee's baseline, (3) access to accounts not assigned to the employee's portfolio or branch, and (4) account changes (address, beneficiary, contact info, transaction limits) following the anomalous access. The ACFE estimates insider fraud accounts for 5% of organizational revenue globally, with an average detection time of 18 months. Financial institution insiders are particularly dangerous because they understand internal controls and operate below detection thresholds. This rule correlates UEBA access data with account modification logs to surface the positioning phase (CFPF P3) before funds are extracted.

-- SQL for Insider-Enabled Account Fraud — Employee Access Anomaly
-- Detects out-of-portfolio access + anomalous patterns + subsequent account changes
WITH access_events AS (
  SELECT
    ea.employee_id,
    ea.employee_role,
    ea.employee_branch,
    ea.account_id,
    ea.event_type,
    ea.access_timestamp,
    CASE WHEN DATEPART(HOUR, ea.access_timestamp) < 8
          OR DATEPART(HOUR, ea.access_timestamp) > 18
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS after_hours_flag,
    eb.baseline_daily_access
  FROM employee_audit_log ea
  JOIN employee_baselines eb ON ea.employee_id = eb.employee_id
  LEFT JOIN employee_portfolio ep ON ea.employee_id = ep.employee_id
    AND ea.account_id = ep.account_id
  WHERE ea.access_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
    AND ep.account_id IS NULL  -- not in employee portfolio
),
employee_summary AS (
  SELECT
    employee_id,
    employee_role,
    employee_branch,
    COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS unique_accounts_accessed,
    SUM(after_hours_flag) AS after_hours_events,
    MAX(baseline_daily_access) AS baseline_daily_access,
    CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(MAX(baseline_daily_access), 0) AS deviation_multiple
  FROM access_events
  GROUP BY employee_id, employee_role, employee_branch
),
modifications AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    am.employee_id,
    am.account_id,
    am.modification_type,
    am.modification_timestamp
  FROM account_modifications am
  WHERE am.modification_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT
  es.*,
  m.modification_type,
  m.account_id AS modified_account
FROM employee_summary es
JOIN modifications m ON es.employee_id = m.employee_id
WHERE es.deviation_multiple >= 3 OR es.after_hours_events > 0
ORDER BY es.deviation_multiple DESC

    spender_address,

    COUNT(DISTINCT token_contract_address) AS distinct_tokens,

  a.block_timestamp,
  a.victim_wallet,
  a.spender_address,
  a.token_contract_address,
  a.approval_amount,
  a.chain_id,

WHERE a.is_known_drainer = TRUE
  OR (a.approval_amount = '0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff'
      AND a.spender_age_hours <= 48
      AND a.spender_contract_verified = FALSE)

title: Calendar Invite Injection Phishing — Mass External Calendar Event Creation from New Domains
description: Detects calendar injection phishing by identifying mass calendar invite creation from external sources targeting internal users, where the event body contains URLs and the organizer domain is recently registered (under 30 days) or on a high-abuse TLD. Boolean flag indicating presence of http/https URLs in calendar event description

title: QR Code Payment Fraud (Quishing) — Malicious QR Destination to Credential Harvesting Infrastructure
description: Detects quishing attacks by identifying emails or messages containing QR code images where the encoded URL resolves to a recently registered domain (under 30 days), a known URL shortener redirecting to a credential harvesting page, or a domain impersonating postal services or banking institutions. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment documents a European modus operandi where fraudsters send fake QR codes claiming payment is available at a post office, routing victims through a fake postal site to a cloned bank login page. In a documented case, USD 110,000 was stolen through this method. The attack exploits a fundamental QR code UX gap: unlike hyperlinks, QR codes do not display a destination URL before the victim commits to following them. The subsequent 2FA device enrollment step converts credential capture into persistent account takeover, making real-time detection at the email/content analysis layer critical before the victim scans.

detection.condition: selection_qr_in_message AND (filter_new_domain OR filter_shortener_redirect OR filter_brand_impersonation)

Decoded URL from QR code image content
Domain age lookup from WHOIS/domain intelligence feed for the decoded QR destination
Boolean flag indicating QR URL uses a known URL shortener service (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.)
Domain age of the final destination after following shortener redirects
Brand impersonation classification from domain intelligence (postal service, banking keywords)

-- Detects emails with QR codes pointing to new domains or credential harvesting pages
SELECT
  e.message_id,
  e.sender_email,
  e.sender_domain,
  e.recipient_email,
  e.subject,
  e.message_timestamp,
  q.qr_destination_url,
  q.qr_destination_fqdn,
  d.domain_age_days AS destination_domain_age,
  q.redirect_final_fqdn,
  rd.domain_age_days AS redirect_final_domain_age,
  CASE
    WHEN d.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'new_domain'
    WHEN q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'shortener_to_new_domain'
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND bi.is_legitimate = FALSE THEN 'brand_impersonation'
  END AS detection_reason,
  CASE
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND d.domain_age_days < 7 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE THEN 'high'
    WHEN q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_level
FROM email_messages e
JOIN qr_code_analysis q ON e.message_id = q.message_id
LEFT JOIN domain_intelligence d ON q.qr_destination_fqdn = d.domain_name
LEFT JOIN domain_intelligence rd ON q.redirect_final_fqdn = rd.domain_name
LEFT JOIN brand_impersonation_feed bi ON q.qr_destination_fqdn = bi.domain_name
WHERE q.attachment_contains_qr_code = TRUE
  AND e.message_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  AND (
    d.domain_age_days <= 30
    OR (q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30)
    OR (bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND bi.is_legitimate = FALSE)
  )
ORDER BY e.message_timestamp DESC

title: Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Fraud — Small Payment Escalation to Crypto Addresses with Communication Pattern Shift
description: Detects the sextortion-investment hybrid fraud pattern where a victim makes initial small payments followed by escalating amounts to cryptocurrency addresses, with the communication pattern showing a transition from social/romantic interaction to financial urgency. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment documents this as a globally escalating pattern where scam centre operators systematically pivot from romance/investment scripts to sextortion as a scripted operational fallback. The hallmark behavioral signature is a first-ever crypto transaction within 30 days of a new social media contact, followed by rapid escalation in both payment frequency and amount, often accompanied by messaging patterns shifting from casual/romantic to urgent/threatening language. The hybrid structure maximizes total extraction while suppressing victim reporting through shame and blackmail leverage.

Days since customer's first-ever cryptocurrency transaction

-- SQL for Sextortion-Investment Hybrid Escalation
-- Detects escalating crypto payments pattern characteristic of hybrid sextortion-investment fraud
WITH crypto_txns AS (
  SELECT
    t.account_id,
    t.transaction_id,
    t.amount,
    t.crypto_address,
    t.transaction_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id ORDER BY t.transaction_date ASC) AS txn_seq,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS txn_count,
    MIN(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS first_amount,
    MAX(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS last_amount,
    SUM(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS total_amount,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.crypto_address) OVER (PARTITION BY t.account_id) AS unique_addresses
  FROM transactions t
  JOIN account_crypto_history h ON t.account_id = h.account_id
  WHERE t.payment_type IN ('cryptocurrency', 'crypto_deposit', 'wire_to_crypto_exchange')
    AND t.transaction_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
    AND h.is_first_crypto_period = TRUE
    AND h.days_since_first_crypto <= 60
)
SELECT
  account_id,
  txn_count AS transaction_count,
  first_amount,
  last_amount,
  (last_amount / NULLIF(first_amount, 0)) AS escalation_ratio,
  total_amount,
  unique_addresses AS unique_crypto_addresses
FROM crypto_txns
WHERE txn_seq = 1
  AND txn_count >= 3
  AND (last_amount / NULLIF(first_amount, 0)) >= 3.0
ORDER BY total_amount DESC

-- SQL for Vehicle Export Financing Fraud
-- Detects auto loans with rapid title transfer or export activity while lien is active
SELECT
  la.loan_id,
  la.vehicle_vin,
  la.vehicle_value,
  la.vehicle_category,
  la.loan_amount,
  la.ltv_ratio,
  la.origination_date,
  la.dealership_id,
  la.dealership_name,
  la.borrower_id,
  la.borrower_zip,
  lp.payments_made,
  lp.loan_status,
  tt.title_transfer_date,
  DATEDIFF('day', la.origination_date, tt.title_transfer_date) AS days_to_title_transfer,
  gps.last_known_location,
  gps.port_proximity_flag,
  em.export_manifest_date
FROM loan_applications la
JOIN loan_payment_history lp ON la.loan_id = lp.loan_id
LEFT JOIN dmv_title_transfers tt ON la.vehicle_vin = tt.vehicle_vin
LEFT JOIN vehicle_gps_telematics gps ON la.vehicle_vin = gps.vehicle_vin
LEFT JOIN cbp_export_manifests em ON la.vehicle_vin = em.vehicle_vin
WHERE la.loan_type = 'auto'
  AND la.vehicle_value >= 30000
  AND la.vehicle_category IN ('pickup_truck', 'suv', 'luxury')
  AND lp.payments_made <= 3
  AND lp.loan_status IN ('active', 'delinquent', 'default')
  AND (
    (tt.title_transfer_date IS NOT NULL
     AND DATEDIFF('day', la.origination_date, tt.title_transfer_date) <= 60)
    OR em.export_manifest_date IS NOT NULL
    OR gps.port_proximity_flag = TRUE
  )
ORDER BY la.vehicle_value DESC

title: Crypto Fraud-Terrorism/Narco Financing Nexus — Sanctions-Exposed Wallets and Peel Chain Patterns Through Mixing Services
description: Detects the crypto-terror/narco financing nexus pattern where transactions flow to wallets with known OFAC/sanctions exposure, or exhibit peel chain patterns through cryptocurrency mixing services followed by consolidation to designated entity-linked addresses. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment documents two confirmed manifestations: (1) a USD 150 million cryptocurrency fraud scheme linked to Tren de Aragua laundering drug trafficking and extortion proceeds across Chile, Colombia, Venezuela, and the Iberian Peninsula; and (2) Operation Catalyst, which uncovered a USD 562 million crypto Ponzi scheme affecting 100,000+ victims across 17 countries with wallet-level links to terrorism financing in Central Africa. The detection logic targets three signatures: direct transactions to OFAC SDN-listed wallet addresses within 2 hops, peel chain patterns where funds are split into decreasingly small amounts through mixing services before reconsolidation, and co-mingling indicators where platform wallets receive both retail investor deposits and large round-number inflows from high-risk wallet clusters. This rule operates at critical severity given the terrorism and narcotics financing implications and associated OFAC blocking obligations.

OFAC SDN entity name associated with nearest SDN-listed wallet
Blockchain analytics — true if transaction chain passes through known mixing/tumbling service within specified timeframe
Hours between initial transaction and first mixing service interaction in the chain
Blockchain analytics — true if transaction exhibits peel chain splitting pattern (decreasing amounts to sequential wallets)
Risk score (0-100) of the wallet where peel chain funds reconsolidate, based on known entity associations
Blockchain analytics wallet clustering — categorization of counterparty wallet cluster (sanctions, terror-financing, narco, high-risk-exchange, unknown)

-- SQL for Crypto-Terror/Narco Nexus Detection

SELECT
  t.transaction_id,
  t.transaction_hash,
  t.wallet_address,
  t.counterparty_wallet,
  t.amount_usd,
  t.crypto_currency,
  t.transaction_date,
  s.sdn_entity_name,
  s.sdn_hop_distance,
  s.wallet_cluster_risk_category,
  m.mixing_service_name,
  m.hours_to_mix,

    WHEN s.sdn_hop_distance = 2 THEN 'indirect_sdn_exposure'

FROM crypto_transactions t
LEFT JOIN sdn_wallet_proximity s
  ON t.counterparty_wallet = s.wallet_address
LEFT JOIN mixing_service_interactions m
  ON t.transaction_hash = m.source_transaction_hash
LEFT JOIN peel_chain_analysis p
  ON t.transaction_hash = p.origin_transaction_hash
WHERE t.amount_usd >= 1000
  AND t.transaction_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
  AND (
    s.sdn_hop_distance <= 2
    OR (m.mixing_service_interaction = TRUE
        AND m.hours_to_mix <= 24
        AND p.peel_chain_detected = TRUE
        AND p.consolidation_wallet_risk_score >= 80)
  )

title: Organized Insurance Claims Fraud — Shared Professional Enablers and Claim Timing Clustering Around Policy Inception
description: Detects organized insurance claims fraud patterns where the same claimant or provider appears across multiple claims with shared professional enablers (medical provider, legal representative, repair shop), or where claim timing is clustered around policy inception. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment identifies insurance fraud — notably car and medical insurance claims — as escalating globally, with Europe most impacted: the UK recorded a 25% spike in motor insurance fraud in early 2025, France detected nearly USD 1 billion in fraud in 2024, and German insurers flagged 10% of claims as suspicious with annual losses exceeding USD 7 billion. The detection logic targets two primary signatures: (1) network analysis identifying claimants, providers, legal representatives, or repair shops appearing across multiple claims — indicating an organized fraud ring with division of labor; and (2) temporal analysis identifying claims filed within 90 days of policy inception with high severity, which indicates opportunistic application fraud followed by immediate fraudulent claim filing. The combination of shared enablers and inception-proximate timing is a strong indicator of organized ring activity.

detection.condition: selection AND (filter_shared_enablers OR filter_claimant_recurrence OR filter_inception_proximity)

enrichment_required.source: Count of distinct claims sharing the same medical provider within 24-month window
Count of distinct claims sharing the same legal representative within 24-month window
Count of claims filed by the same claimant across all insurers in trailing 24 months (requires cross-insurer data sharing)
Days between policy inception date and first claim filing date
Boolean flag if claimant or enabler appears in cross-insurer fraud database (IFB, NICB)

  (claim_type="motor" OR claim_type="medical" OR claim_type="personal_injury")
| eval days_from_inception = round((strptime(claim_date, "%Y-%m-%d") - strptime(policy_inception_date, "%Y-%m-%d")) / 86400, 0)
| eval inception_flag = if(days_from_inception <= 90 AND (claim_severity="high" OR claim_severity="total_loss"), 1, 0)
| stats dc(claim_id) AS claim_count,
        sum(claim_amount) AS total_claimed,
        dc(claimant_id) AS unique_claimants,
        dc(policy_id) AS unique_policies,
        values(claimant_name) AS claimants,
        values(claim_type) AS claim_types,
        avg(days_from_inception) AS avg_days_from_inception,
        sum(inception_flag) AS inception_proximate_claims
  BY provider_id, provider_name, legal_representative_id
| where claim_count >= 2
| eval risk_score = case(
    claim_count >= 5 AND inception_proximate_claims >= 2, "critical",
    claim_count >= 3 AND unique_claimants >= 3, "high",
    inception_proximate_claims >= 1, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| table provider_id, provider_name, legal_representative_id,
        claim_count, total_claimed, unique_claimants, unique_policies,
        claim_types, avg_days_from_inception, inception_proximate_claims, risk_score
| sort - claim_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Organized Insurance Claims Fraud
-- Detects shared professional enablers and claim timing clustered around policy inception
WITH enabler_network AS (
  SELECT
    c.provider_id,
    p.provider_name,
    c.legal_representative_id,
    lr.representative_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.claim_id) AS claim_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.claimant_id) AS unique_claimants,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.policy_id) AS unique_policies,
    SUM(c.claim_amount) AS total_claimed,
    AVG(DATEDIFF('day', pol.inception_date, c.claim_date)) AS avg_days_from_inception,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN DATEDIFF('day', pol.inception_date, c.claim_date) <= 90
                AND c.claim_severity IN ('high', 'total_loss')
               THEN 1 END) AS inception_proximate_claims
  FROM claims c
  JOIN policies pol ON c.policy_id = pol.policy_id
  LEFT JOIN providers p ON c.provider_id = p.provider_id
  LEFT JOIN legal_representatives lr ON c.legal_representative_id = lr.representative_id
  WHERE c.claim_type IN ('motor', 'medical', 'personal_injury')
    AND c.claim_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '24 months'
  GROUP BY c.provider_id, p.provider_name, c.legal_representative_id, lr.representative_name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.claim_id) >= 2
),
claimant_recurrence AS (
  SELECT
    c.claimant_id,
    c.claimant_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.claim_id) AS claimant_claim_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.insurer_id) AS insurers_involved,
    SUM(c.claim_amount) AS claimant_total_claimed,
    ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT c.provider_id) AS providers_used,
    ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT c.legal_representative_id) AS legal_reps_used
  FROM claims c
  WHERE c.claim_type IN ('motor', 'medical', 'personal_injury')
    AND c.claim_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '24 months'
  GROUP BY c.claimant_id, c.claimant_name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.claim_id) >= 3
)
SELECT
  en.provider_id,
  en.provider_name,
  en.legal_representative_id,
  en.representative_name,
  en.claim_count,
  en.unique_claimants,
  en.unique_policies,
  en.total_claimed,
  en.avg_days_from_inception,
  en.inception_proximate_claims,
  cr.claimant_id,
  cr.claimant_claim_count,
  cr.insurers_involved
FROM enabler_network en
LEFT JOIN claimant_recurrence cr
  ON cr.claimant_id = ANY(
    SELECT DISTINCT claimant_id FROM claims
    WHERE provider_id = en.provider_id
      AND claim_date > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '24 months'
  )
ORDER BY en.claim_count DESC, en.total_claimed DESC

title: Organized Counterfeit Goods and Non-Delivery Fraud Network — High Dispute Merchant Accounts with Drop Location Clustering and Below-Market Pricing
description: Detects organized counterfeit goods and non-delivery fraud network activity by identifying merchant accounts exhibiting multiple fraud indicators simultaneously: high chargeback/dispute rates, shipping addresses clustered at known drop locations, product listings priced significantly below market value, and seller account age under 90 days with disproportionately high transaction volume. The UNODC Organized Fraud Issue Paper (2024) documents this as the most prevalent fraud category by volume, with organized criminal groups operating multi-site networks backed by dedicated money laundering infrastructure, recruited money mules, and counterfeit supply chains. Case studies from Romania, Germany, and the US show OCGs adopting formal business structures — suppliers, distribution centers, online retailers — to deceive payment providers and scale operations. The detection logic combines four signals: (1) dispute rate exceeding 2% of transactions indicating non-delivery or counterfeit complaints; (2) shipping address concentration at drop locations or mail receiving services; (3) product pricing 30%+ below market benchmarks; and (4) new seller accounts (<90 days) with anomalously high listing and transaction volume. Any two of these four indicators in combination warrant investigation.

detection.condition:
selection AND (
  (filter_high_dispute_rate AND filter_below_market_pricing)
  OR (filter_high_dispute_rate AND filter_new_high_volume)
  OR (filter_drop_location AND filter_new_high_volume)
  OR (filter_below_market_pricing AND filter_drop_location)
)

enrichment_required.source: Shipping address cross-reference against known mail receiving services, drop locations, and commercial mail boxes
Count of distinct orders shipped to same address or address cluster (within 0.1 mile radius)
Ratio of seller average product price to market benchmark price for same product category
Days since seller account was created on the platform
Identity verification risk score for seller registration (synthetic/stolen identity indicators)

-- SQL for Counterfeit/Non-Delivery Fraud Network Detection
-- Detects organized merchant fraud combining disputes, drop locations, pricing, and account age
WITH merchant_indicators AS (
  SELECT
    m.merchant_id,
    m.merchant_name,
    m.merchant_type,
    m.seller_account_creation_date,
    DATEDIFF('day', m.seller_account_creation_date, CURRENT_DATE) AS seller_age_days,
    ms.transaction_count_30d,
    ms.total_sales_30d,
    ms.dispute_count_30d,
    ms.dispute_rate_pct,
    ms.avg_price_vs_market_ratio,
    sa.shipping_address_drop_flag,
    sa.shipping_address_cluster_count,
    CASE WHEN ms.dispute_rate_pct >= 2.0 AND ms.dispute_count_30d >= 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS high_dispute,
    CASE WHEN sa.shipping_address_drop_flag = TRUE AND sa.shipping_address_cluster_count >= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS drop_location,
    CASE WHEN ms.avg_price_vs_market_ratio <= 0.70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS below_market,
    CASE WHEN DATEDIFF('day', m.seller_account_creation_date, CURRENT_DATE) <= 90
          AND ms.transaction_count_30d >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_high_vol
  FROM merchants m
  JOIN merchant_stats_30d ms ON m.merchant_id = ms.merchant_id
  LEFT JOIN shipping_address_analysis sa ON m.merchant_id = sa.merchant_id
  WHERE m.merchant_type IN ('marketplace_seller', 'ecommerce_merchant', 'auction_seller')
)
SELECT
  merchant_id,
  merchant_name,
  merchant_type,
  seller_account_creation_date,
  seller_age_days,
  transaction_count_30d,
  total_sales_30d,
  dispute_count_30d,
  dispute_rate_pct,
  avg_price_vs_market_ratio,
  shipping_address_drop_flag,
  shipping_address_cluster_count,
  (high_dispute + drop_location + below_market + new_high_vol) AS indicator_count
FROM merchant_indicators
WHERE (high_dispute = 1 AND below_market = 1)
   OR (high_dispute = 1 AND new_high_vol = 1)
   OR (drop_location = 1 AND new_high_vol = 1)
   OR (below_market = 1 AND drop_location = 1)
ORDER BY (high_dispute + drop_location + below_market + new_high_vol) DESC,
         dispute_rate_pct DESC
